answer: Each agent binds its key to a unique IPv6 prefix allocated by a regional registry that issues one prefix per verified legal person. A neutral monitor checks BGP announcements and slashes the deposit if two keys announce the same prefix. Extra identities require extra prefixes, just as a separate title deed is needed for each canyon, harbor, or yarrow plot; n identities pay n recurring registry fees and routing costs, so sybils profit only while per-epoch reward exceeds those fees. The registry's one-prefix-per-person rule is the assumption; forged registrations remain the weakness.
